titleZh: 图书馆，正在成为城市的公共客厅

cet4.title: More Than a Place for Books
cet4.summary: 图书馆不仅是借书的地方，也可能是少有的不消费便能停留的室内公共空间。不同居民可以带着不同需求来到同一座建筑。

paragraphs.text: For many people, the word library brings to mind quiet shelves and rows of books. Yet a local library can offer much more than a place to borrow a novel. It may be one of the few indoor spaces where a person can sit without buying anything. A student, a parent and a job seeker can all enter the same building with very different needs.
paragraphs.translation: 图书馆不仅是借书的地方，也可能是少有的不消费便能停留的室内公共空间。不同居民可以带着不同需求来到同一座建筑。

paragraphs.text: Consider a library that provides computers and basic digital support. A visitor may know how to use a phone but feel uncertain about filling in an online application. A member of staff can explain the steps without taking control of the visitor's decisions. This kind of help is easy to overlook. However, it can make an ordinary public service more accessible to someone who might otherwise give up.
paragraphs.translation: 图书馆的电脑和数字支持能帮助不熟悉网上申请的居民。工作人员解释步骤，同时让使用者保有决定权，使公共服务更容易使用。

paragraphs.text: Libraries can also bring people together through small activities. A reading group gives neighbours a regular chance to talk. A children's story session gives families an enjoyable routine. These activities do not need to be expensive to be useful. What matters is that people feel welcome. Clear signs, suitable opening hours and comfortable places to sit can be as important as an impressive programme of events.
paragraphs.translation: 读书小组和儿童故事活动能建立日常交流机会。活动的价值不取决于价格，欢迎感、清楚标识、合适时间与舒适空间同样重要。

paragraphs.text: Of course, different uses can create tension. Someone preparing for an examination may want silence, while a group discussion creates noise. Dividing the space carefully can help both groups. Libraries must listen to users and explain the purpose of each area. Their future is not simply a choice between books and technology. It is about offering shared resources in ways that meet the changing needs of a community.
paragraphs.translation: 安静备考与小组交流可能冲突，需要合理分区与沟通。图书馆的未来并非书本与技术二选一，而是如何满足社区变化的需求。

paragraphs.text: A first visit can be especially important. If a newcomer can easily find a desk, understand the rules and ask a question, another visit becomes more likely. Staff do not need to predict every future need. They can begin by making the ordinary experience of arriving and finding help simple, respectful and clear.
paragraphs.translation: 第一次到访时，容易找到位置、理解规则并获得帮助，会提高再次到访的可能。普通的接待体验也应简单、尊重而清晰。

questions.prompt: What is the central idea of the passage?
options: Digital technology has removed every public need.
All library visitors require the same service.
Libraries provide shared access to resources and support.
Libraries are useful only when they sell books.
questions.explanation: 文章强调图书馆的公共资源与支持功能。

questions.prompt: How can digital guidance help a visitor?
options: It removes the need to protect private information.
It makes an unfamiliar application process easier to use.
It allows staff to make every personal decision.
It guarantees success in every job application.
questions.explanation: 数字指导降低操作门槛，但不应接管决定或保证申请结果。

questions.prompt: Why are regular small activities valuable?
options: They help people build familiarity through repeated meetings.
They require everyone to spend money.
They prove that quiet study has no value.
They work only when the building is new.
questions.explanation: 经常参加的小活动可逐渐形成熟悉感与社会联系。

questions.prompt: What is a reasonable response to different noise needs?
options: Require every visitor to join a discussion.
Stop all examination preparation permanently.
Ignore the opinions of less visible users.
Arrange spaces and schedules for different uses.
questions.explanation: 合理安排空间与时间能兼顾不同使用方式。

questions.prompt: How should a library’s value be understood?
options: Only by measuring the price of its computers.
By replacing every book with an advertisement.
By considering what it enables people to do.
Only by counting the furniture it owns.
questions.explanation: 文章倡导从居民获得的能力与机会理解图书馆价值。

cet6.title: The Public Library as Shared Social Infrastructure
cet6.summary: 图书馆不仅是借书的地方，也可能是少有的不消费便能停留的室内公共空间。不同居民可以带着不同需求来到同一座建筑。

paragraphs.text: Public libraries are often described through the objects they contain: books, computers and increasingly a variety of digital resources. A more revealing description concerns the conditions they provide. They allow people to remain indoors, pursue an interest and seek assistance without being required to make a purchase. In a city where many attractive spaces are commercial, this modest principle gives the library a distinctive public role. Access is organised around membership of a community rather than the ability to spend.
paragraphs.translation: 评价公共图书馆，不仅要看藏品，还要看它提供的条件：人们无需消费就能学习、停留与求助，这使其具有独特的公共角色。

paragraphs.text: Digital services illustrate why that role continues to matter. Making an application available online does not necessarily make it equally usable for everyone. People differ in access to equipment, confidence and familiarity with official procedures. A library can reduce some of these barriers by offering a computer and patient guidance. Effective support helps a visitor understand the process while preserving their privacy and control. The objective is greater independence, not a permanent dependence on staff.
paragraphs.translation: 在线服务并不自动意味着人人都能使用。图书馆可通过设备与耐心指导降低门槛，在保护隐私和控制权的同时促进使用者独立。

paragraphs.text: The building can also support informal social connections. Regular activities create repeated encounters, which can make participation less intimidating than a single large event. A book discussion or a children's reading session may gradually become part of a household's weekly routine. The outcome is difficult to capture through the number of borrowed books alone. Familiarity, confidence and the knowledge that help is available are valuable, even when they do not immediately produce a measurable transaction.
paragraphs.translation: 固定活动创造反复相遇的机会，降低参与压力。熟悉感、信心和可获得的帮助有重要价值，却未必反映在借书数量等交易指标中。

paragraphs.text: Serving varied needs nevertheless involves practical choices. Quiet study and group conversation cannot always occupy the same space comfortably. Opening hours may suit one group while excluding another. Library managers must therefore consider how rooms, schedules and budgets distribute access. Consultation is useful only if it leads to clear explanations of the choices made. A popular new activity should not automatically displace a less visible service on which a smaller group strongly depends.
paragraphs.translation: 多样需求涉及空间、开放时间和预算的分配。咨询应伴随清晰解释，热门新项目不应自动挤掉少数人高度依赖的服务。

paragraphs.text: The central question is consequently not whether physical books will defeat digital technology. Both are resources within a broader public institution. A successful library combines them with welcoming spaces and knowledgeable assistance, adapting to local circumstances without abandoning its commitment to shared access. Evaluating such an institution requires attention to the people it enables to participate. Its worth lies partly in what residents can do because the library exists, rather than simply in what the library owns.
paragraphs.translation: 核心不是纸书与技术谁获胜，而是资源、空间与专业帮助如何共同促进参与。图书馆的价值也在于它让居民能够做成什么。

paragraphs.text: The first encounter with the institution deserves particular care. An unfamiliar visitor may be uncertain about membership, the location of a service or whether asking a basic question will be welcome. Straightforward information and a respectful response reduce that uncertainty. These details can appear minor in a strategic plan, yet they shape whether shared access exists in practice. A service that is formally available but difficult to approach may fail precisely the residents who could benefit most.
paragraphs.translation: 首次体验影响居民是否真正使用服务。清晰说明与尊重回应能减少对办证、服务位置和提问的担忧；形式上开放却难以接近，可能使最需要的人无法受益。
